title: Computation is not a basic physical property

statements.text: Computation is not a basic physical property of a system: calling a system a computation depends on a description or a purpose brought to it. The frameworks that say so put it differently: a computation names no present physical property its different hardware shares, or computation is execution with a goal that someone sets.

sources.quote: These implementations need share no evident intrinsic physical property corresponding to the computation they implement

The burden therefore falls on proponents of digital consciousness to identify an observer-independent present physical invariant shared across these materially and geometrically disparate implementations.
It is only one specific type of execution: execution with a goal.
A computer program computes because someone defines input, output, and purpose.
If our universe has no goal, then how can everything be computation?
